en: The Sūtra of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Bodhisattva Tārā,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Mingjiao Dashi,
the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Tianxi Cai, at the Gulmavilāsa Monastery in the kingdom of Jālandhara, Central India.
With single-minded devotion, I take refuge and pay homage to Mount Potalaka, the most auspicious and delightful,
whose realm is adorned with various precious jewels and diverse groves of jewel-trees.
Branches and vines hang down thickly, adorned with various kinds of accomplished *kusu* flowers;
their radiant light shines everywhere,
and there are various ponds and pools with the sounds of diverse flowing springs.
There are also various forms: the fragrance of elephants, the king of deer, and the wondrous song of the bee-king;
the beautiful melodies of kinnara maidens and the music performed by gandharvas;
as well as noble devas and human beings.
The Sage, free from desire, is constantly gathered therein with the assembly of other bodhisattvas,
as well as the noble Tārā Bodhisattva who possesses mastery over the ten stages,
together with a thousand vidyā-queens.
Surrounded by the Wrathful Great Vidyārājas, such as Hayagrīva and others,
at that time the noble and virtuous Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
having completed his great practices for the benefit of all sentient beings, was fully endowed [with all qualities].
The one endowed with loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity, dwelling within that womb,
gives birth upon a seat of auspicious lotuses; sitting there calmly and upright,
he preaches the sublime Dharma to the great assembly of humans and devas.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Greatly Powerful Wrathful King,
out of compassion for others, asked Avalokiteśvara about lions,
elephants, tigers, snakes, water, fire, thieves, and shackles.
How can sentient beings who are indolent and inferior escape these eight difficulties?
Long dwelling in the ocean of saṃsāra,
they are bound by the fetters of saṃsāra— greed, hatred, and delusion.
"If they are made to attain liberation, I shall declare that the Muni is one who is honored by the world. At that time,
Avalokiteśvara uttered a sublime and beautiful voice, awakening Vajrapāṇi.
Listen well, Lord of Secrets!
Born from my vow for a lifespan of no weight, I am the Mother of all worlds;
holding an utpala lotus in my hand, I emit light that illuminates this realm.
Throughout the world of humans and devas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others were struck with awe;
they cried out, "Do not be afraid!
We have manifested through the Buddha's transformative power to protect the world."
Amidst various perils and terrors— The fears of war, famine,
and the cycle of saṃsāra— I rescue sentient beings;
Therefore, the world calls me Tāra, And speaks of me as the Son of the Buddha.
"Excellent! You should be revered. Having spoken these words, he immediately joined his palms, leaped into the air, and remained suspended there.
With the radiance of his body blazing intensely, he then proclaimed these words: "These are the one hundred and eight names."
This was spoken by the Buddhas of the past; The ten stages, the masteries, and the immeasurable bodhisattvas— Upon hearing this, they give rise to joy.
If there are those who receive and uphold it, All their transgressions will be completely eliminated.
May merit increase and fame spread; may wealth and all auspiciousness abound.
May all illnesses be utterly dispelled, and may one dwell in tranquility within the field of merit.
May there be longevity and peace, and may one give rise to loving-kindness to deliver sentient beings.
He is named the Great Sage; possessing such virtues, he thus spoke.
Avalokiteśvara smiled and surveyed the ten directions, manifesting transformations and exercising a compassionate mind; he then extended his right hand.
With arms adorned by the marks of merit, he addressed that one of great wisdom, saying:
"Excellent, Vajrapāṇi! Now listen to this name of Great Merit, which is wondrously tranquil; it shall be taught directly to people."
If one hears [this], one shall obtain peace and happiness, Abundant wealth along with sovereignty;
One shall be liberated from all illnesses And be endowed with all meritorious virtues.
Untimely death shall be extinguished, And after passing away, one shall be born in Sukhāvatī.
O gods and others, you should know: listen attentively as I now speak.
You should all rejoice deeply; I shall proclaim these one hundred and eight names, known as the "One Hundred and Eight Names of Peaceful Secrecy."
Capable of benefiting all sentient beings, this rare and secret field of merit is found neither among gods nor humans;
it is exceedingly difficult to encounter,
yet it enables all sentient beings who behold it to attain peace and happiness.
The wise person should with single-mindedness bathe and purify their body;
by reciting with focused mindfulness throughout the three periods of the day,
that person will before long gain the love and respect of the king, and leaving suffering behind, attain peace and happiness.
The poor obtain wealth and treasure; The foolish attain great wisdom and intelligence, no longer harboring doubt. From shackles they find liberation;
from defeat they turn to victory. Enemies in turn become virtuous friends.
Sharp fangs and keen horns, quarrels and strife,
and various perils and fears— by recollecting this name,
one can be rescued from all such terrors, and the end of life shall be brought to rest.
One’s fame shall spread far and wide, and one will always be born into a noble and virtuous lineage;
being such a singular individual, whether walking, sitting, or lying down,
one shall receive the praise of others and attain a long life.
May humans receive happiness, as well as devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, pūtanas,
kaṭapūtanas, duṣṭa-mātṛs, strī-grahas, and ḍākinīs.
The Uṣṭrās, and others; the epileptic spirits and the shoulder-walkers;
the great ghosts, Vetālas, and Nāginīs;
and all other beings of evil intent—none dare to overstep its shadow.
How much less can those of violent and evil nature—
through battlefields, incantations, or illusory arts—
harm one who possesses sovereignty and majesty, nor their descendants or their property.
Increasing boundlessly, one attains the supernormal power of recollecting past lives;
noble clans see them with joy. Possessing unimpeded great eloquence, they thoroughly comprehend all treatises and meanings; thus they encounter virtuous friends.
Adorning the Bodhicitta: A Sūtra of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Tārā Bodhisattva for Constantly Approaching All Buddhas and Praising Their Holy Virtues Throughout Successive Lifetimes.
